paper_title: On the Runtime of Local Mutual Exclusion for Anonymous Dynamic Networks
classifications: Software and its engineering → Mutual exclusion
statement: In future work, it would be interesting to establish a lower bound revealing whether this locking time bound is tight; if so, it remains an open question whether any algorithm exists for local mutual exclusion whose locking time is free of dependence on the size of the dynamic network.
context: The adversarial scheduler considered in this paper selects an arbitrary subset of enabled nodes at any stage, and each activated node randomly selects one of its enabled actions executions. An alternative that would yield similar expected times as the ones proven here would be to have each node keep a FIFO queue of its enabled action executions, where action executions are inserted into the queue, and executed, in the order they become enabled, and are removed from the queue if they get disabled. Note that, while the choice of action execution now becomes deterministic, the runtime bound of the algorithm would still be probabilistic, given the use of randomization in the algorithm. Another alternative approach would be to change the guards of the actions to induce a set of “priorities” over the enabled action executions (guaranteeing that certain action executions would only be enabled after “higher priority” action executions are all disabled). However, this does not work within the structure of actions of the algorithm in [17], since any fixed priority approach applied to the current algorithmic structure leads to the “starvation” of some action executions and prevents progress. In future work, it would be interesting to establish a lower bound revealing whether this locking time bound is tight; if so, it remains an open question whether any algorithm exists for local mutual exclusion whose locking time is free of dependence on the size of the dynamic network.
